reviewNote: Drafted by Claude from the chart for faculty review. Not validated teaching content.
summary: Strabismus surgery in a 9 y with trisomy 21, repaired AV canal, known atlantoaxial instability (ADI 5 mm in flexion) and a new report of tripping more, which needs a neuro exam before he is positioned. Also oculocardiac reflex, sevoflurane bradycardia history, mild OSA, emergence delirium and high PONV risk.

asa.rationale: Trisomy 21 with repaired congenital heart disease, atlantoaxial instability, OSA.

decision.recommendation: neuro exam first; proceed if normal
decision.rationale: New gait change in a child with atlantoaxial instability may be early myelopathy. If the exam shows any new deficit, delay for MRI and neurosurgery review. If normal, proceed with neck precautions.

redFlags.finding: Atlantoaxial instability with possible new symptoms
redFlags.evidence: ADI 5 mm in flexion (2024); mother says he trips more lately; tumbling and trampoline.
redFlags.implication: Cord injury with neck flexion during laryngoscopy or positioning.
redFlags.action: Focused neuro exam, neutral neck, avoid flexion, video laryngoscopy; MRI and delay if deficits.

redFlags.evidence: Medial rectus surgery; bradycardia with sevoflurane 8% in 2022; first degree AV block.
redFlags.implication: Severe bradycardia or asystole with muscle traction.
redFlags.action: Glycopyrrolate or atropine ready or given, avoid high sevoflurane concentrations, ask surgeon to release traction.

redFlags.evidence: Mild residual OSA; prior grade 1 to 2; nasal congestion.
redFlags.implication: Obstruction at induction and emergence; possible subglottic narrowing.
redFlags.action: Smaller cuffed ETT ready, oral airway, observe postop.

redFlags.evidence: Wild wake up 2022; anxious; midazolam ordered.

redFlags.implication: Possible MH susceptibility signal if trismus with succinylcholine.
redFlags.action: Avoid succinylcholine, monitor EtCO2 and temperature.

planItems.item: Mask induction after oral midazolam, then IV
LMA or cuffed ETT with neutral neck
Observe for OSA; overnight if desaturations
